title: Oncall simulation deck and HTTP failure injector
author: Priya Narang
description:
Motivation: On-call training and realistic incident rehearsals are time consuming to setup and often unreproducible. This PR introduces a compact 'simulation deck' format and a controlled HTTP failure injector that together let SREs and on-call engineers replay real-world failure scenarios deterministically against a sandboxed environment.

What this adds: a) simctl CLI (incident-bot/cmd/simctl) to compose and run simulation decks; b) a deck manifest format (YAML) that encodes alert traces, latency distributions, downstream-5xx profiles, and deterministic RNG seeds for reproducible runs; c) an HTTP failure injector implemented as a Kubernetes Job and lightweight Envoy filter snippets (applied to a temporary simulation sidecar) to create controlled 4xx/5xx and latency-injection traffic shaping; d) integration hooks that emit simulation traces/metrics tagged with sim_id for SLO impact calculations in slo-toolkit; e) safety guardrails: dry-run mode, namespace isolation, quota checks, a conservative circuit-breaker (max 5 concurrent sim jobs), and an automatic cleanup/finalizer to revert Envoy filters and remove the job.

Safety and scope: The injector runs only in a namespaced simulation sandbox by default (--namespace=oncall-sim-<id>), refuses to target production namespaces, and requires the operator to pass an allowlist file for clusters where simulations are permitted. The default behavior is a no-op dry-run until an explicit --confirm flag is provided. All injected metrics use a "sim." prefix and an exported sim_id label so telemetry is segregated.

Usage (short): simctl init-deck --from-trace trace-2026-01-12.json 
then simctl run --deck example-deck.yaml --confirm --namespace oncall-sim-42 --seed 12345

Test plan: unit tests for deck parsing and RNG deterministic behaviour, e2e integration tests in the canary sandbox cluster (runs as part of integration CI), and a staged runbook exercised during dogfood week that validated cleanup and observability tagging.

Risks and mitigations: initial integration test flakiness was due to job cleanup races; added exponential backoff and a finalizer to ensure Envoy filter removal. Destructive failure injection prevented by explicit allowlist and require-confirm semantics.

Why now: reproducible, fast on-call exercises help reduce MTTR; this gives teams a low-effort way to rehearse specific customer-impacting traces and verify SLO alerting and runbooks end-to-end.

release_notes: Added simctl + simulation-deck format and a controlled HTTP failure injector for on-call rehearsals. Includes sandbox e2e tests and observability hooks for SLO impact analysis.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: injector defaults to dry-run and an allowlist; teams should run simulations in the designated sandbox cluster. Followup PRs will add a web UI and a library of curated decks derived from past incidents.
